candidates.text: The purpose of this functionality is to establish a controlled, transparent, and auditable Material Requirements Planning (MRP) approval process within the ERP or production management system.
These requirements ensure that the MRP approval process is controlled, efficient, and auditable, aligning with procurement and production planning goals.
Rejected or held lines are handled systematically with visibility on their impact on the BOM.

Business Requirement:
1. All material lines go through proper approval workflows before procurement.
2. Rejected or held lines are handled systematically with visibility on their impact on the BOM.
3. The system supports incremental updates, minimizing rework and re-approval of unchanged items.
4. Clear segregation of responsibilities and traceability for approvals, rejections, and holds.
5. Improved accuracy in indent generation and material planning through structured validations and controls.
6. A user-friendly UI with expandable views and checkbox selections, enabling efficient decision-making.

Functional Requirements:
1. Need a new Approval permission in user group. I.e., MRP.
2. It will be multi-level approval.
3. We also need to handle the multi-level approval from the Multi-Level Approval Settings only.
When user click on Run MRP in the BOM then system will open up the screen of Material planning screen to validate the all necessary details.
Before sending it to the approval screen, the user must first review and validate the material details in the screen below.
This will be work based on the MRP approval permission is enabled.
Once this action is completed, the system will display the approval popup and automatically load the user list according to the approver configured as a default.
If only a single user is associated with the approver, the system will automatically select that user.
Whenever an approval is defined, the MRP will be routed for approval whenever the user attempts to run it.

Functional Requirements:
1. If the user revises the cost sheet and there are changes in BOM lines that are currently on Hold, and the user sends them again for approval, the system will display the action tool in disabled mode for those specific lines on the approval screen.
2. To enable action tool for these lines, the user must first mark them as 'Ready for Processing' and then resend them for approval. Only after this step will the checkboxes become enabled for selection and approval.

To handle situations where an assigned approver is unavailable, we are introducing a Re-Assign MRP Approval functionality.
Assume that the approval workflow for user A is configured with two possible approvers: X and Y.
If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.

Functional Requirements:
1. User A submits an MRP approval request.
2. The system routes the request to Approver X as per the configured sequence.
3. If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A.

Functional Requirements:
1. When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A.
2. From there, User A will have the ability to re-assign the pending request from X to Y.
3. This allows the originator (A) to redirect the approval to the next available approver.
If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen.

Functional Requirements:
1. If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen.
2. User X will have an option to re-assign the approval request to Y.
3. This supports approver-level delegation.
Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability.

Functional Requirements:
1. Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability.
2. The approval process remains flexible and efficient.
3. Both the requester (A) and the approver (X) have the authority to re-route approval to the next eligible approver (Y).

candidates.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior

candidates.text:
Key Observations & System Behavior:
1. Rejections and Red Lines: Rejected lines are indicated with a red line in the BOM, making it easy to identify which lines have been disapproved by the MRP approval board.
2. Default Checkbox Behaviour: The system automatically ticks lines that are part of the MRP plan for approval (even rejected ones). Lines that are rejected or marked as awaited are unticked or displayed differently in the approval workflow.
3. Awaited Lines Handling: When lines are marked as "awaited," they are excluded from the approval process (checkbox is unticked). Once they are unawaited, they are considered for approval, and their checkbox is ticked.
4. Incremental Changes: When new materials are added (line 7), only the newly added line appears for approval, implying that the system tracks incremental changes and doesn’t resubmit the entire BOM for approval unless changes are made to multiple lines.
5. Indent Generation: Once approval is given, the system generates indents for all lines, which are essentially action requests for procurement or production.
6. Cost Sheet Revision: A revision to the cost sheet can trigger updates to the MRP and require a new approval cycle.
candidates.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior

15. Introducing the MRP Approval Re-Assignment Feature
To handle situations where an assigned approver is unavailable, we are introducing a Re-Assign MRP Approval functionality.
Scenario Overview
Assume that the approval workflow for user A is configured with two possible approvers: X and Y.
• User A submits an MRP approval request.
• The system routes the request to Approver X as per the configured sequence.
• If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
New Solution: Re-Assign Approval
To avoid such delays, we are introducing a provision that allows the approval request to be reassigned from one approver to another.
Re-Assignment Options
Option 1: Re-Assign from “Approval Pending with Others”
• When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A.
• From there, User A will have the ability to re-assign the pending request from X to Y.

chunks.title: Functional Requirements
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements
chunks.text:
• This allows the originator (A) to redirect the approval to the next available approver.
Option 2: Re-Assign from “Approval Pending” by the Approver
• If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen.
• User X will have an option to re-assign the approval request to Y.
• This supports approver-level delegation.
Benefit
This feature ensures that:
• Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability.
• The approval process remains flexible and efficient.
• Both the requester (A) and the approver (X) have the authority to re-route approval to the next eligible approver (Y).

chunks.title: Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process
chunks.text:
This case study revolves around a Bill of Materials (BOM) in an MRP (Material Requirements Planning) system and its approval workflow. The scenario describes how the system handles rejections, approvals, line adjustments, and updates throughout the MRP process.
Here’s a detailed breakdown of each stage: -
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process

chunks.title: Step 1: Adding Materials to the BOM
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 1: Adding Materials to the BOM
chunks.text:
• Initially, 6 material lines are added to the BOM.
• Once the materials are defined, an MRP (Material Requirements Plan) is generated. This plan reflects the materials required for production based on the BOM.
• After generating the MRP, it is sent for approval.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 1: Adding Materials to the BOM

chunks.title: Step 2: Rejection of Lines from MRP Approval
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 2: Rejection of Lines from MRP Approval
chunks.text:
• The MRP approval board reviews the plan, but 5-6 lines are rejected.
• In the system, rejected lines are displayed with a red line against their respective material lines (lines 5 and 6).
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 2: Rejection of Lines from MRP Approval

chunks.title: Step 3: Regenerating the MRP and Sending for Approval
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 3: Regenerating the MRP and Sending for Approval
chunks.text:
• After rejection, the MRP is regenerated for all 6 lines, meaning that the material lines (5-6) are now part of the new plan.
• The system now defaults with checkboxes for all lines (including the rejected ones). By default, lines 5-6 are checked.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 3: Regenerating the MRP and Sending for Approval

chunks.title: Step 4: Unticking Line 5 and Rejecting Again
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 4: Unticking Line 5 and Rejecting Again
chunks.text:
• Line 5 is unticked by the user (indicating that it’s no longer part of the approval request).
• Line 5 is then rejected.
• In the BOM, the system shows a red line against line 6 only, since line 5 was explicitly removed (unticked) and rejected, while line 6 remains rejected.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 4: Unticking Line 5 and Rejecting Again

chunks.title: Step 5: Regenerating MRP and Sending for Approval
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 5: Regenerating MRP and Sending for Approval
chunks.text:
• The user regenerates the MRP and sends it for approval again.
• Upon resending, the system automatically ticks lines 5-6 by default, which means they are still considered in the plan for approval.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 5: Regenerating MRP and Sending for Approval

chunks.title: Step 6: Rejecting Line 5-6 Again
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 6: Rejecting Line 5-6 Again
chunks.text:
• The user rejects both lines (5 and 6) again from the MRP approval dashboard.
• As a result, the system shows red lines against lines 5-6, reflecting that both lines have been rejected again.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 6: Rejecting Line 5-6 Again

chunks.title: Step 7: Marking Line 4 as Awaited
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 7: Marking Line 4 as Awaited
chunks.text:
• The user marks line 4 as "awaited" (perhaps pending further details, approval, or additional checks).
• When the MRP approval is sent, the system now showing the checkbox in line 4 because it is awaited.
• The system shows checkboxes for all other lines except line 4, while lines 5-6 are still default ticked.
• Awaited lines are typically excluded from the approval process, but the checkbox for the line is still shown as unticked.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 7: Marking Line 4 as Awaited

chunks.title: Step 8: Marking Line 4 as "Ready For process"
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 8: Marking Line 4 as "Ready For process"
chunks.text:
• After further processing, line 4 is marked as "Ready for process" (indicating it’s now ready for approval).
• The user then resends the MRP for approval.
• The system now ticks all checkboxes, including line 4, and lines 5-6 remain default ticked.
• All lines are included in the approval process, and the system assumes they are ready to be processed for approval.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 8: Marking Line 4 as "Ready For process"

chunks.title: Step 9: Approving All Lines
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 9: Approving All Lines
chunks.text:
• The user proceeds to tick all checkboxes and approves all the lines via the MRP approval dashboard.
• After approval, the system generates indents for all material lines. These indents are requests for the materials to be purchased or prepared for production based on the approved BOM.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 9: Approving All Lines

chunks.title: Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)
chunks.text:
• After the indents are generated and the cost sheet is revised, the user adds a new material (line 7) to the BOM.
• The user regenerates the MRP to include the new material.
• Upon sending for approval again, the system only shows line 7 (the new material) in the approval request.
• This suggests that the system recognizes the new line (line 7) as the only change to the MRP after the last approval cycle, and it requires separate approval for the new material.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)

chunks.title: Key Observations & System Behavior
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior
chunks.text:
• Rejections and Red Lines: Rejected lines are indicated with a red line in the BOM, making it easy to identify which lines have been disapproved by the MRP approval board.
• Default Checkbox Behaviour: The system automatically ticks lines that are part of the MRP plan for approval (even rejected ones). Lines that are rejected or marked as awaited are unticked or displayed differently in the approval workflow.
• Awaited Lines Handling: When lines are marked as "awaited," they are excluded from the approval process (checkbox is unticked). Once they are unawaited, they are considered for approval, and their checkbox is ticked.
• Incremental Changes: When new materials are added (line 7), only the newly added line appears for approval, implying that the system tracks incremental changes and doesn’t resubmit the entire BOM for approval unless changes are made to multiple lines.
• Indent Generation: Once approval is given, the system generates indents for all lines, which are essentially action requests for procurement or production.
• Cost Sheet Revision: A revision to the cost sheet can trigger updates to the MRP and require a new approval cycle.
chunks.locator: § Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior

chunks.title: Conclusion
chunks.heading: Functional Requirements › … › Conclusion
chunks.text:
The MRP system facilitates the approval workflow by allowing users to manage individual lines in the BOM, reject materials, mark lines as awaited, and approve changes incrementally. It ensures transparency by displaying red lines for rejected items, and it supports efficient approval and indent generation processes by focusing on only the modified lines when new changes are introduced.
This structured approval and material planning process helps maintain accuracy in the procurement and production cycles, especially when dealing with multiple materials and frequent updates.
